properties.headline: Tornado Warning issued October 10 at 6:01PM EDT until October 10 at 6:30PM EDT by NWS Columbia SC
properties.description:
At 601 PM EDT, a confirmed tornado was located near Aiken State Park,
or 16 miles northeast of Aiken, moving north at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Damaging tornado.

SOURCE...Radar confirmed tornado.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is
likely.

Locations impacted include...
New Holland and Steedman.

This includes Interstate 20 in South Carolina between mile markers 30
and 36.
properties.instruction:
To repeat, a tornado is on the ground. TAKE COVER NOW! If you are
outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to an interior room
or closet on the lowest floor of a sturdy building immediately.

dust.

* WHERE...Northern Lander and Northern Eureka, Northern Elko, and
Humboldt Counties.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hazardous driving conditions due to reduced visibility.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 2:47PM PDT until October 14 at 4:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.4 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Pablo Bay.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical. Dangerous conditions are
forecast along the shoreline. Hazards include sneaker waves,
strong rip currents, and large breaking waves.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.4 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:18 PM
Sunday 10/11, 1.2 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:46 PM
Monday 10/12, 1.1 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 1:14 PM
Tuesday 10/13, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.7 ft MLLW) at 1:46 PM
Wednesday 10/14. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 3:44PM MDT until October 12 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, Central Mountains, Eastern Juab/Millard Counties, San
Rafael Swell, Sanpete Valley, Sevier Valley, Wasatch Plateau/Book
Cliffs, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef National Park and
Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell, South Central
Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper Sevier River Valleys, Western
Canyonlands, Lower Washington County, Southwest Utah and Zion
National Park. This also includes recent burn scars such as
Forsyth, Cottonwood, Silver King, France Canyon, and Monroe Canyon.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may
occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Anomalously high moisture is forecast to impact the region with
the arrival of the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel. While this
is expected to be a long duration rainfall event, scattered
instances of heavier rainfall rates are expected with stronger
storms yielding flash flooding concerns given saturated soils and
prior burn scars.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Desert and Mountains, Northern Wasatch Front, Salt Lake Valley,

Uinta Basin and Western Uinta Mountains. This includes recent burn

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and recent burn scars. Flooding may occur in poor
drainage and urban areas. Extensive street flooding and flooding of

will move into northern Utah this weekend producing a prolonged
rainfall event. In particular, moisture interacting with a
frontal boundary across far northern Utah may yield locally
heavier rainfall totals compared to other locations. As a result,
areal flooding is expected across northern Utah this weekend.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 10 at 5:35PM EDT until October 10 at 6:15PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
SMWJAX

The National Weather Service in Jacksonville has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine FL out 20
NM...
Waters from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine FL from 20 to 60
NM...

* Until 615 PM EDT.

* At 535 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 8 nm east of Jacksonville Beach, or 24 nm
north of Saint Augustine, moving northeast at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Anna Reef.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes. If your vessel is
caught offshore, immediately secure for heavy weather. Ensure all
crew members are wearing USCG approved Type I life jackets and
nonessential crew are below decks. Deploy jack lines and harnesses if
available. Check life saving equipment, including batteries on
handheld radios, for readiness.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately. If your vessel is caught offshore, immediately secure
for heavy weather. Ensure all crew members are wearing USCG approved
Type I life jackets and nonessential crew are below decks. Deploy
jack lines and harnesses if available. Check life saving equipment,
including batteries on handheld radios, for readiness.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Minor saltwater flooding of low elevation streets and
lots is likely. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater. In addition, in the Upper
Keys, Bayside communities will likely see little to no relief
from flooding even at low tide.
properties.instruction: Do not drive through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 5:33PM EDT until October 10 at 6:30PM EDT by NWS Columbia SC
properties.description:
At 533 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 3 and 4.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
North Augusta, Augusta, Fort Gordon, Clearwater, Belvedere,
Hephzibah, South Augusta, Glendale, Daniel Field, Summerville,
Midtown, Augusta Mall, Augusta Regional Airport, Augusta National
Golf Club, Village Plaza Shopping Center, McBean, Gloverville and
Burnettown.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 520 in South Carolina between mile markers 16 and 23.
Interstate 20 in South Carolina between mile markers 0 and 7.
Interstate 20 in Georgia between mile markers 195 and 201. Interstate
520 in Georgia between mile markers 1 and 15.
properties.instruction:
Most flooding deaths occur in vehicles. Never drive through a flooded
roadway or around barricades. Turn around, don't drown.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
